1. Leave granted.
2. The High Court of Orissa at Cuttack by the impugned judgment and order dated 30th May, 2025 has rejected the appellants prayer for bail.

entities.text: High Court of Orissa at Cuttack
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
3. The appellant figures as an accused in FIR No. 0131 of 2022 dated 11th March, 2022 registered with Police Station-Town, District:
Dhenkanal, Odisha is in custody since 14 th March, 2022.

It is alleged in the FIR that the appellant committed offence(s) punishable under Section(s) 4, 5 and 6 of the Prize Chits and Money Circulation Schemes (Banning) Act, 1978, Sections 120-B, 34,
406, 420, 467, 468, 471 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, and Section 6 of the Odisha Protection of Interests of Depositors (In Financial Establishments) Act, 2011.

entities.label: STATUTE

entities.text: Odisha Protection of Interests of Depositors (In Financial Establishments) Act, 2011
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 4. We have heard learned counsel appearing for the parties and perused the materials on record.
5. The trial has commenced.

Out of thirty three witnesses the prosecution proposes to examine,
evidence of only nine witnesses has been recorded till date.

6. Our attention has been drawn to a previous order dated 12 th November, 2024 passed by a coordinate Bench while considering the prayer for grant of bail of a co-accused, i.e., Pallavi Mishra Satyaranjan Hota vs State Of Odisha on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98512490/
1 @ Pallavi Hota, who happens to be the wife of the appellant.

entities.text: Pallavi Mishra Satyaranjan Hota vs State Of Odisha on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
While rejecting the prayer for release on bail, this Court had granted liberty to the said petitioner (Pallavi Mishra) to renew her prayer for bail before the High Court if no substantial progress of the trial is achieved by the end of January,
2025.
7. We are at the end of the year.
In our considered view, having regard to the pace of progress of the trial, an early conclusion seems to be remote.
Having regard to the long incarceration together with the nature of allegations levelled and the stage of the trial

, we are inclined to accept the appeal.
8.
Accordingly, we set aside the impugned judgment and order.
9. The appellant shall be released on bail, subject to such terms and conditions as may be imposed by the trial court.
10. We clarify that the observations made in this order and grant of bail will not be treated as findings on the merits of the case.
The appeal is, accordingly, allowed on the aforesaid terms.
13. Pending application(s), if any, stand disposed of.
